item.title: Every week without fail, 31st October
item.description:
Persistent littering and overflowing rubbish bins There is a persistent problem with rubbish and litter being left around the communal bins in the street. Bin bags are regularly ripped open, with waste spilling out and spreading across the pavement. As shown in the attached photographs, rubbish, food waste, plastic bags and other discarded items are scattered across the pavement and surrounding area. The bins are overflowing, and the problem appears to be ongoing rather than a one-off incident. This creates an unpleasant and unhygienic environment for residents and pedestrians. It also obstructs the pavement and can attract vermin. Please investigate this ongoing issue and arrange for the area to be cleared. I would also ask the council to review the frequency of rubbish collection and consider measures to prevent bin bags from being ripped open and rubbish from repeatedly accumulating in this location. This is a recurring problem that requires a lasting solution, rather than occasional clean-ups.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Woodland Grove, Greenwich

item.title: Persistent rubbish dumping, rodent activity and serious public health hazard on main road, 31st October
item.description:
The persistent accumulation of rubbish at this location is absolutely disgraceful and unacceptable. This is an ongoing problem that Southwark Council has failed to address effectively. As the photograph shows, large quantities of waste are being dumped directly onto the pavement along a busy main road. The Council's apparent solution has been to install a large litter bin, which has clearly done nothing to resolve the problem. There is now rodent activity nearby, raising serious public health and sanitation concerns. The rubbish is also accumulating beside tactile paving at a pedestrian crossing, creating potential hazards for pedestrians, particularly those with visual impairments. This is a disgusting eyesore and an embarrassment to the borough. Residents should not have to tolerate filthy pavements, dumped waste and rodents in their neighbourhood. Whether the waste originates from nearby businesses, residents or both, the Council must investigate and take meaningful enforcement action. I expect immediate removal of the rubbish, thorough cleaning, investigation of the rodent activity, identification of those responsible and a permanent solution to prevent further dumping. Residents pay council tax and deserve clean, safe public spaces. Simply clearing the rubbish whenever complaints are made is NOT a sustainable solution. Southwark Council must take responsibility for addressing this recurring environmental health concern and explain what lasting preventative action will be taken. The continued neglect of this location is completely unacceptable.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 49, Boyson Road, Walworth, Greater London

item.title: Cyclists not stopping at red light, 31st October
item.description:
I am writing to raise a serious concern regarding the increasing number of cyclists, particularly riders using Lime bikes, who are routinely jumping red traffic lights and putting pedestrians at risk. On the evening of 31 October, I witnessed a particularly concerning incident while crossing the road. A cyclist ignored a red traffic light and rode through the junction, almost knocking over a child who was crossing at the same time as me. This was an extremely dangerous situation that could easily have resulted in a serious injury. Unfortunately, this is not an isolated incident. I have personally had several near misses involving cyclists failing to stop at red lights, and I am increasingly concerned about the risks this behaviour poses to pedestrians. The issue appears especially prevalent among users of hire bikes, including Lime bikes, whose riders seem to disregard traffic signals and pedestrian right of way. This behaviour is particularly dangerous for vulnerable road users, including children, elderly pedestrians and disabled people, who may not be able to react quickly enough to avoid an oncoming cyclist. Pedestrians should be able to cross the road safely without having to anticipate cyclists ignoring traffic signals. I would therefore like to understand what measures are being taken to address this issue, including enforcement against cyclists who disregard red lights and whether further measures can be introduced to improve pedestrian safety. If Lime bikes are contributing to this problem, I would also like to know what action is being taken to ensure their users comply with road traffic regulations. I appreciate that cycling is an important mode of transport, but this should not come at the expense of pedestrian safety. There needs to be greater accountability and enforcement before a preventable incident results in someone being seriously injured. I look forward to receiving a response outlining what action will be taken to address these concerns.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 33, Dalston Lane, Dalston, Greater London
